tour.title: Project Purpose
tour.description: Begin with the repository README and project context to orient yourself to FT Transcendence and the Nook product. The documentation index then points to the maintained project and service guides, giving you a map for the rest of the tour.

tour.title: Local Service Stack
tour.description: Building on that overview, the Compose definition shows how the application services, networks, and persistent dependencies are assembled for local operation. The Compose guide and environment-file guide explain how to approach setup and service-specific configuration, while the example variables illustrate the User service's database, broker, mail, and bootstrap settings.

tour.title: User Service
tour.description: With the runtime context established, the User service guide explains the service's responsibilities, data ownership, and operational behavior. Its setup guide and NestJS bootstrap file connect those responsibilities to how the service is configured and started.

tour.title: Accounts and Identity
tour.description: The User service's Prisma schema makes its persistent domain concrete, covering accounts, social relationships, images, authentication providers, and token-related models. The OpenAPI document describes the HTTP contract that lets the client use these capabilities without depending on the database representation.

tour.title: Chat Service
tour.description: The chat overview explains how messaging fits into the product and summarizes the service's feature direction. The chat service's NestJS entry point is the concrete start of its server, building on the separate account and identity responsibilities introduced in the previous steps.

tour.title: Messaging Data and API
tour.description: The chat schema models groups, direct conversations, channels, messages, read state, and reactions, showing the data structures behind the messaging features. Its OpenAPI specification presents the HTTP operations and request and response contracts that expose those features to other parts of the system.

tour.title: Web Client Shell
tour.description: After learning the two backend domains and their contracts, turn to the Next.js client that presents the product to users. The client guide describes its runtime and API-routing expectations, while the shared layout defines the page shell, metadata, and global providers used across the interface.

tour.title: Behavior and Regression Tests
tour.description: Tests show how important behaviors are checked at the service and interface boundaries established earlier in the tour. The User service accounts test covers success, validation, and failure cases, the chat service test checks interactions with gateways and persistence, and the client theme test protects token contrast and accessibility expectations.
